summary: Ambiguous microbatch rate applied to multi-model microbatch job causing invoice overcharge
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports what appears to be an overcharge on invoice INV-2026-03-09-4842 for a scheduled microbatch job that routed mixed-model requests in a single job. Customer believes the billing engine applied a single (higher) per-token rate to the entire microbatch instead of computing a weighted cost across model variants, leading to an overcharge of approximately $1,250.

Impact:
- Invoice INV-2026-03-09-4842 shows a single line for 'microbatch-processing' for job_id cb-job-19f8 with 10,234,000 tokens billed at $0.00012/token.
- Customer claims the job included 6.7M tokens for redwood-13b-v2 (rate $0.00006/token) and 3.534M tokens for open-llama-7b-q4 (rate $0.00012/token). If billed correctly, expected charge is $6.7M * 0.00006 + 3.534M * 0.00012 = $402 + $424 = $826 (approx), but invoice shows $1,228 (approx), delta ~$402.

Request:
- Immediate provisional credit to cover the delta while we investigate.
- Adjustment to final invoice if bug confirmed.

Customer contact: alice.chen@cognifylabs.ai (CC: finance@cognifylabs.ai)
steps_to_reproduce: Customer runs scheduled microbatch job (cb-job-19f8) that contains mixed requests routed to two models in one job window.
Serving runtime batches requests across models when possible for throughput optimization.
Metering postback aggregates batch-level token counts and looks up per-model rates to produce invoice lines.
Observed behavior: postback created a single invoice line using a single per-token rate of $0.00012 for the entire aggregate instead of splitting by model or computing weighted average.
impact: Customer-facing invoice discrepancy (charged ~49% more than expected for the microbatch job). Potential financial impact for Cognify Labs and reputational risk for Redwood. Customer requests provisional credit and corrective invoice adjustments.
comments: 2026-03-10 | Sofia Patel (Support): Acknowledged receipt and opened ticket. Asked for invoice PDF and raw postback payload. SLA flagged P1; provisional credit requested.

2026-03-10 | Alice Chen (Customer): Attached invoice INV-2026-03-09-4842 and a CSV export of job_id cb-job-19f8 with per-request model assignments and token counts. Requested credit for delta $402.00 and asked for timeline.
2026-03-11 | Ethan Myers (Billing): Requested raw metering postback logs (S3 path) and the job grouping key. Requested runbook link for postback processing. Marked as Sev1 for billing investigation.

2026-03-12 | SRE (R. Alvarez): Found postback file s3://redwood-metering/postbacks/2026/03/09/cb-job-19f8/postback.json; initial parsing shows aggregated 'token_total' and a single 'applied_rate' field. Hypothesis: aggregation routine chooses the highest model rate when resolving multi-model batches.
2026-03-13 | Billing (Ethan Myers): Issued provisional credit note: CR-2026-03-13-359 for $402.00 applied to Cognify Labs account. Pending final reconciliation after root cause analysis.
2026-03-14 | Alice Chen (Customer): Confirmed provisional credit applied and asked for a written postmortem and timeline for fix and possible historical corrections if other invoices affected.
2026-03-14 | Sofia Patel (Support): Noted customer request for postmortem and added to follow-up actions.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11: Retrieved job CSV from customer and compared token counts to postback payload. Totals match: 10,234,000 tokens. Customer-specified per-model splits also match sampling (6,700,000 for redwood-13b-v2, 3,534,000 for open-llama-7b-q4).
2026-03-11: Examined metering postback pipeline. Postback processor groups rows by batch_id and resolves an 'applied_rate' by calling rate_resolution.lookup(batch_rows).

2026-03-12: rate_resolution.lookup implementation (preliminary): it fetches distinct model_rate values from rows and currently returns max(model_rate) when more than one distinct rate exists. This seems to be defensive logic intended to avoid undercharging but it is incorrect for microbatch-level aggregation. See code reference: platform/billing/postback/resolve_rates.py (line ~142).

2026-03-12: Confirmed similar pattern in historical postbacks for mixed-model jobs (sampling last 30 days). Found 7 other accounts with mixed-model microbatches where applied_rate was set to max(model_rate) producing overcharges ranging $12-$1,100. Aggregated exposed overcharge across sampled accounts: ~$2,465. Need a full audit to quantify total exposure.

2026-03-13: Created internal issue INT-5021 to coordinate a rollback and audit. Short-term mitigation: adjust postback processor to emit split invoice lines per model when batch contains multiple model_rate values (PR created).

2026-03-13: Drafted PR for fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7124 — change rate_resolution.lookup to compute weighted average or emit per-model invoice lines. PR passes unit tests; integration tests in staging scheduled 2026-03-15.

2026-03-14: Confirmed provisional credit was applied for Cognify Labs. Preparing communications: (1) root cause summary, (2) timeline for rollout, (3) plan for historical invoice corrections and outreach.
resolution: Provisional credit CR-2026-03-13-359 of $402.00 applied on 2026-03-13. Root cause identified: postback rate resolution used the maximum model rate when multiple rates were present, causing overcharge for mixed-model microbatches. Fix implemented in PR #7124 to emit per-model invoice lines (or weighted average where appropriate). Integration testing in staging scheduled for 2026-03-15; production rollout planned for 2026-03-16 with a follow-up billing audit to identify all affected invoices in the last 90 days. Customer will be notified with a postmortem and a list of any historical invoice adjustments.
